findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any file error (not found, permissions, I/O).
findings.failure_mode: untrusted file path aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle.
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use .map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e)) to surface I/O failures.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value in the second CSV field.
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line with non-numeric value in column 2 aborts the entire batch instead of returning a typed parse error.
findings.fix: use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| LoadError::Invalid(line_num)) and return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>.

findings.problem: as u16 conversion after parse silently truncates values > 65535.
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 like 70000 parses successfully then truncates to 4448, producing silently corrupt domain data.
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| LoadError::Overflow(line_num)) to reject out-of-range values.

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] use unchecked indexing into a split result collected into Vec.
findings.failure_mode: a CSV line with fewer than 2 fields (empty line, trailing newline, malformed row) panics via index-out-of-bounds.
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and match on Some((name, value_str)) with .ok_or(LoadError::Invalid(line_num)).

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) embeds side-effecting I/O inside the parsing/mapping closure.
findings.failure_mode: pure data-loading function leaks console I/O into the functional core, making the function non-deterministic, untestable in isolation, and impossible to use in contexts where stdout capture or silence is required.
findings.fix: remove println entirely from the pure path. If logging is needed, return a separate log/warning type or push it into the shell layer after load_sessions returns.

findings.problem: load_sessions fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing (split/collect), domain construction (Record), and side-effecting I/O (println) into a single function.
findings.failure_mode: no separation of concerns prevents testing pure parsing independently of filesystem state; callers cannot substitute in-memory data, mock files, or reuse the parsing logic without triggering disk access.
findings.fix: split into (1) fn parse_record(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> for pure logic and (2) fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> for shell work that reads the file and calls parse_record.

findings.problem: Vec::with_capacity is absent; split+collect creates intermediate Vec with unbounded allocation from untrusted file content.
findings.failure_mode: a file with millions of lines or extremely long lines allocates unbounded heap memory, enabling OOM DoS from hostile input.
findings.fix: validate line count against a trusted cap before allocation; use iter().map(...).try_reserve(cap).map_err(...); then collect into Vec, or use a streaming approach.

findings.problem: split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a Vec for all CSV fields and trims every one, when only two fields are needed.
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation per line plus allocation of trimmed copies for every field, even unused ones; also splits on ALL commas so a name containing commas corrupts the record.
findings.fix: use let (name, value_str) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) then parse only value_str.

findings.problem: load_sessions returns Vec<Record> with no error type; all failures are panics (unwrap, indexing, cast).
findings.failure_mode: callers cannot distinguish file-not-found from malformed data from numeric overflow, preventing targeted recovery or reporting.
findings.fix: define enum LoadError { Io(std::io::Error), Invalid(usize), Overflow(usize) } and return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>.

findings.problem: Record::name is a raw String with no invariants enforced by the type system.
findings.failure_mode: any code can create Record with empty, whitespace-only, or otherwise invalid names, making illegal domain states representable.
findings.fix: use a Name newtype with a smart constructor: struct Name(String); impl Name { fn new(s: &str) -> Result<Self, ParseError>; }

findings.problem: No benchmarks, baseline measurements, or profiler evidence exist for load_sessions performance characteristics.
findings.failure_mode: performance claims about this function are unsubstantiated; unbounded allocation on hostile input is unquantified.
findings.fix: add criterion or similar benchmarks measuring I/O latency, per-line parsing throughput, and allocation profiles across small/large/hostile inputs.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sessions throughput or allocation
no baseline measurement for file size vs allocation profile
no profiler data (flamegraph, heaptrack, or similar) on current implementation
no second-ring evidence: no Miri, Kani, or loom runs for UB/concurrency concerns in file I/O paths
no command evidence: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy, cargo check, cargo test were not run (review-only mode, no edit permission)
residual_risk: Static review only. Every function in this crate violates absolute laws (unwrap, unchecked indexing, lossy cast, hidden I/O, fused shell/core). No commands were run. A full Holzman-compliant rewrite would need: typed errors, split_once parsing, remove all unwrap/panic, remove println from pure path, introduce newtypes, bounded allocation with try_reserve, and separate pure parser from I/O shell. Without running cargo check/clippy/test, no guarantee of compile-correctness or test coverage.
